acs.text: On a package detail page that accepts submissions, the onboarding seat select lists only seats still available this month.

expected_answer.operand: each onboarding seat option is still available this month

judgements.rationale: Applied money, user-reach, and change-frequency because onboarding seats are a shared monthly capacity tied to a priced package; misrendering this list can overbook inventory and affect every submitting author.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because the manuscript-status options gate every submission and are likely to change with content or form implementation updates.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because the default genre prompt is shown to every author and incorrect defaults can mislead or block completion across the submission surface.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because the default manuscript-status prompt affects every author using the form and is vulnerable to UI or copy regressions.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because the book-title input is a core field required for every submission and any form-layout regression would affect all authors.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because the author-name input is a core field required for every submission and any form-layout regression would affect all authors.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because the email input is a core field required for every submission and any form-layout regression would affect all authors.
Applied money, user-reach, and change-frequency because the onboarding-seat control is part of shared capacity allocation on a priced package and must remain present and functional for all authors.
